# Independent audit: two-shape compatibility and discrete-base Green cone



Source: `candidate ed6a06822db211dc`.
Verifier: `supporting computation verify_chain_green_support_cone_coherent.py`.


and verifier. After two clarifications described below, the final
verifier reran with **33,985 exact rational checks**. The arbitrary-N,
arbitrary-d assertions rest on the mathematical proof, not these
finite checks. The exact deformation cone and its regular derivative
dual are established; no favorable descent sign or general OC claim
is asserted.

## 1. Two-shape support compatibility

The support of (1-theta_p)A+theta_p B is h_A+theta_p Delta. All
anchored Minkowski inclusions are therefore equivalent to the
displayed sign inequality. These inclusions imply actual sections
of the hull because every point at an integer base has an anchored
convex representation. Completeness of the finite base excludes
additional integer bases.

Nonnesting means that Delta has both signs, forcing equality of
the scalar coefficient difference. Proper containment gives one
nonnegative support difference that is positive somewhere, hence
exactly the stated one-sided sampled concavity. On a complete
integer interval, preserving adjacent midpoint representations
forces an affine sequence, which then preserves every anchored
barycenter. No stronger affine claim for an arbitrary finite base
is used.

## 2. Fan space and exact one-sided tangent cones

Positive Minkowski coefficients give the common refinement normal
fan F. Thus every interior chain fiber has this exact fan, even
when endpoint fans are coarser. Values on the rays determine the
piecewise linear homogeneous function, subject to the explicitly
retained nonsimplicial consistency constraints in dimensions above
two.

For a function in V_F, testing that every linear piece is below
the function at every ray suffices: rays positively generate each
cone, so the inequality extends across every cone. The function is
then the maximum of its finitely many linear pieces and is exactly
a polytope support function. Conversely, a convex piecewise linear
function has each of its pieces as a global supporting linear form.

At an exact-F support function, every ray outside a given maximal
cone has strict support gap; a ray inside that cone gives an identity
on V_F. Finitely many strict rows therefore persist under arbitrary
small V_F perturbations. At a coarser endpoint, exactly the active
rows impose one-sided linear inequalities on the perturbation.
Inactive rows retain positive gaps. These facts prove the stated
endpoint tangent cones and preserve full dimension for small time.

Pointwise nonnegativity on all rays is equivalent to nonnegativity
everywhere by the same cone generation. C_F is pointed. It is the
full ray-coordinate orthant in dimension two; treating it as such
in higher dimensions without consistency constraints would be
incorrect, and the source does not do so.

## 3. Exact Green factorization and endpoint lineality

Since the initial support sequence is affine at each normal, actual
compatibility of h_j+t delta_j is exactly nonnegative second
differences of delta at every normal. Consecutive concavity implies
all anchored inequalities through the concave piecewise affine
interpolant. Conversely adjacent midpoint inclusions give these
second differences. This uses actual support functions, not only
volume-root concavity.

The kernel min(i,j)(N-max(i,j))/N vanishes at both endpoints and
has discrete second difference one at i and zero elsewhere. The
displayed Green sum therefore has the required curvature and
endpoints. The difference between any two such representations is
affine with zero endpoints, so uniqueness follows. Endpoint support
feasibility plus the unrestricted interior fan tangent space gives
one common positive time for the finite family. Its hull has exactly
the integer bases 0 through N and is a full-dimensional compact body.

For fixed endpoints every interior support velocity is pointwise
nonnegative. A strictly positive curvature value in one direction
propagates to every interior base because every interior Green entry
is positive. This proves the actual coupling constraint and rules
out independent inward motion in that fixed-endpoint cone.

If both signs of eta are feasible at h_A, then on each old fan cone
the functions eta and -eta are convex after subtracting the linear
h_A piece. Thus eta is linear on that cone and belongs to V_(F_A).
Conversely an old-fan perturbation preserves its strict support rows
for both small signs. This proves the endpoint lineality exactly.
Pointedness of C_F forces zero interior curvature in a lineality
direction, giving precisely the harmonic interpolation of the two
old-fan endpoint lineality functions. Translations alone do not
exhaust this space.

## 4. Four-site planar calibration

For the triangle-to-square chain, the five ray support coordinates
give the two indicated new-edge inequalities at the triangle and
the diagonal-truncation inequality at the square. All other old
edges have positive length. Their signs are correct. There are
twenty array coordinates, ten curvature inequalities, and three
nontrivial endpoint tangent inequalities. Endpoint lineality has
dimension three plus four, hence seven.

The two interior Green columns are (2/3,1/3) and (1/3,2/3).
Thus the support-velocity ratio bounds and simultaneous propagation
are exact. Increasing both interior X and Y offsets by t, fixing
the diagonal and the endpoints, has c_1=c_2=1 in each of X and Y
and zero other curvature. It is feasible and outside the original
two-shape coefficient span, whose only varying ray support is the
diagonal. This supplies coupled motions, not a claimed favorable
depth response.

## 5. Mass and fixed-cap first variations

A support-coordinate change delta(r) has normal speed delta(r)/|r|.
The area coefficient H_(d-1)(F_jr)/|r| is therefore correct. Summing
over actual own-fiber facets gives the volume derivative. At a
missing endpoint facet the area is zero and a newly born face has
only higher-order volume contribution. With this fixed finite fan,
candidate vertices move affinely in time, and edge-neighborhood
remainders are controlled as claimed.

For fixed endpoints, nonnegative support velocities give outward
strips. The one-sided cap trace is one on an outward-oriented
coincident cap and zero on an inward-oriented coincident cap. If
the continuous cap normal vanishes, a whole-fiber closed boundary
is retained. Noncoincident boundaries cut only facet-null sets.
Thus the formula covers genuine oblique, supporting, and pure-base
caps without substituting open boundaries. For signed velocities,
the regular formula is used only under the stated exclusion of
facet coincidence.

In the plane, parallel Minkowski edge lengths add, so each area/ray
coefficient is affine in j. The two Green sums and their resulting
mass coefficient are correct. For the four-site example the ten
values in the source agree exactly; the transverse X,Y motion has
total mass derivative two.

The verifier's original three-point quadratic extraction did not
itself certify a stable clipping chamber. Following this audit,
the author added an exact certificate: every pair-intersection
vertex is affine in time, and every remaining inequality slack
has no root in (0,2h]. It checks all ten modes, every fiber, and
every augmented cap system; roots at zero are allowed. Therefore
the right-hand combinatorial chamber is fixed, its polygon area
is exactly quadratic, and the three-point derivative extraction
is rigorous. The final 33,985-check run includes this certificate.

## 6. Regular critical circuits and global depth response

The weighted continuous normals and threshold offsets in (18)
sum to zero, so each group covers its whole anchored continuous
plane. The section coefficients S are assumed positive and
two-sided; availability of such circuits at an arbitrary minimum
is not asserted. Facet transversality is stated for every facet
whose velocity is used, and for all original facets when using
the endpoint cone.

The normalization kappa=(rho/S)/sum(rho/S) makes the proposed
threshold velocities have exactly zero rho-weighted sum. Hence
the whole-plane cover persists, while all group cap masses acquire
the same first derivative T_g. The intersection of a threshold
slab with moving facet strips is o(t) under the stated transversality,
so the combined derivative is legitimate. Nondeepest bases have
explicit finite whole-plane covers with strict mass gaps; their
fixed cap masses vary continuously and preserve the needed bound.

The resulting cap covers bound depth at every point of every new
fiber, not only at the old marked points. Dividing by the varying
total mass gives exactly M^(-1) max_g(T_g-beta M'). The Green
representation gives the stated response formula. Strict negativity
for all groups consequently yields actual descent in this class.

At a local minimum, separating the finite-dimensional response cone
from the open negative orthant supplies one common nonnegative
group multiplier vector pi, normalized to sum one. It applies to
all curvature directions simultaneously. This is a necessary
condition for every selected regular circuit system, not a claim
that one favorable circuit system is sufficient for minimality.

## 7. Endpoint duals and exact relation to earlier roof tests

Full-cone separation gives both the curvature tests and endpoint
tangent tests with the same pi. The source now explicitly writes
the endpoint functionals as

    H_0=sum_j(1-j/N) q_j,   H_N=sum_j(j/N) q_j.

They act on T_A^F and T_B^F respectively. Testing q_0 and q_N alone
would be wrong; the interpolation sums correctly include all
interior propagation. Two-sided lineality forces these functionals
to vanish on the appropriate old-fan spaces.

When both endpoint planar fans are full, arbitrary endpoint ray
values give sum q_j=0 and sum j q_j=0. The interior Green potential
s=G q_int is nonnegative. Applying the discrete inverse gives the
interior equations, and the total and first-moment equations give
q_0=-s_1 and q_N=-s_(N-1). Summation by parts with these exact
endpoint terms proves the converse nonnegative-response condition.

These full-fan planar tests already follow from the earlier
concave-roof tests, exactly as the source says. For one ray r, any
compatible scalar support sequence delta_j(r) has a concave
piecewise affine interpolant on [0,N]. Extending the first and
last slopes makes a global concave polyhedral function. Dividing
by |r| gives a base-only roof on the common ambient supporting
facet, with precisely the required own-fiber normal speed. Affine
sequences provide the two moment identities; the Green hats provide
the nonnegative potentials. Conversely their Green decomposition
generates every such scalar concave sequence. Therefore no stronger
necessary inequality than the full roof tests is claimed here.

The useful additional calculation is the exact finite support-cone
factorization, the propagation through independently locked fibers,
and the explicit handling of coarser endpoint tangent cones and
their lineality. The source keeps those contributions distinct
from an unproved numerical bound or a general descent theorem.

## Scope

The theorem concerns full-dimensional polytopal Minkowski-affine
chains with fixed fan space, and its depth derivative conclusion
has explicit regular circuit and transversality hypotheses. It
does not provide polytopal attainment, structure of arbitrary bad
minima, a sign for every response, or recursive lower-dimensional
boundary stress. Within this exact scope, all statements pass.
